record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For 1s-max smti, where ties occur on only one side of the market, determine whether the current approximation upper bound can be reduced to 5/4.

evidence.quote: It is thus an open problem as to whether this latter upper bound can be reduced to 5/4 in the case of 1s-max smti.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with Ties and Incomplete lists, restricted so that ties occur on only one side of the market (1-sided SMTI). An instance consists of two disjoint finite sets, the men $U$ and the women $W$. Each man $u \in U$ has a strictly ordered preference list over a subset of $W$ (his acceptable partners). Each woman $w \in W$ has a preference list over a subset of $U$ (her acceptable partners) in which ties (groups of equally ranked men) are allowed. A matching $M$ is a set of pairwise disjoint man–woman pairs $(u,w)$ such that each pair is mutually acceptable. A pair $(u,w) \notin M$ is a blocking pair for $M$ if $u$ and $w$ find each other acceptable, $u$ is either unmatched in $M$ or strictly prefers $w$ to his $M$-partner, and $w$ is either unmatched in $M$ or strictly prefers $u$ to her $M$-partner or is indifferent between them. A matching $M$ is weakly stable if it admits no blocking pair. The problem MAX-SMTI with one-sided ties asks for a weakly stable matching of maximum cardinality.

For a constant $c \ge 1$, a polynomial-time algorithm is a $c$-approximation algorithm if, for every instance, it returns a weakly stable matching of cardinality at least $\mathrm{OPT}/c$, where $\mathrm{OPT}$ denotes the maximum cardinality of a weakly stable matching.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial-time $\tfrac{5}{4}$-approximation algorithm for MAX-SMTI with one-sided ties? Equivalently, can the best achievable polynomial-time approximation ratio for this problem be reduced to $5/4$?
artifact.status_search_result: The general one-sided-ties MAX-SMTI approximation ratio has been progressively improved (3/2, then 25/17 ≈ 1.4706 by Iwama–Miyazaki–Yanagisawa, then 22/15 ≈ 1.4667 by Huang–Kavitha, then 13/9 ≈ 1.444 by Bauckholt–Pashkovich–Sanità in 2018), but none reach 5/4. Lam and Plaxton later achieved the 5/4 bound only when tie lengths are bounded by 2 (and more generally an integrality-gap-matching bound for bounded tie size). For unbounded one-sided ties, no 5/4-approximation is known and the question appears to remain open, while 5/4 is the known UGC-hardness lower bound.

status_evidence.title: On the approximability of the stable marriage problem with one-sided ties (Bauckholt, Pashkovich, Sanità)
status_evidence.snippet: Refined analysis giving an improved 13/9-approximation factor for stable marriage with one-sided ties.
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound is 13/9 ≈ 1.444, still above 5/4.

status_evidence.title: A 25/17-Approximation Algorithm for the Stable Marriage Problem with One-Sided Ties
status_evidence.snippet: Improves the previous 1.5 ratio to 25/17 ≈ 1.4706 for MAX-SMTI with one-sided ties.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Stable Matching with One-Sided Ties of Bounded Length
status_evidence.snippet: Lam and Plaxton: for tie length at most L, an approximation 1+(1-1/L)^L matching the integrality gap; in particular 5/4 for ties of size at most 2.
status_evidence.claim: 5/4 achieved only for bounded tie length, not the general problem.
